production.malt: Lagg uses 100% malted barley and produces peated spirit at different specifications, including 20 ppm and 50 ppm runs. Official technical material identifies Concerto malt in established production.
production.fermentation: Four Douglas-fir washbacks, each 24,000 litres and normally filled to 20,000 litres, are used. Current official process material gives approximately 55-60 hours with M-strain distillers yeast, followed by an additional resting period in a pine receiver before distillation.
production.stills: Two custom Forsyths copper pot stills are used: a 10,000-litre bulbous-onion wash still and a 7,000-litre lamp-glass spirit still. The stills are short and broad with a downward-sloping lyne arm, and are steam heated.
production.peat: Lagg is designed around peated whisky production, with official material documenting 20 ppm and 50 ppm malt specifications depending on the production run.
production.maturation: The core Kilmory style is matured in first-fill bourbon barrels; the distillery also uses Oloroso sherry and a range of other finishing casks for specific releases.

houseCharacter: Lagg deliberately uses cloudy wort, M-strain yeast and a moderately long fermentation to retain fatty-acid and ester precursors that contribute earthier, weightier flavours. Its short, broad stills and downward-sloping lyne arms reduce reflux compared with tall-necked designs, reinforcing body and peat weight. The result is a smoky spirit with an oily texture but enough fruit to stop the profile becoming purely tarry or medicinal.
cask23Narrative: Lagg was engineered from the start to make a fuller, earthier style of peated Arran whisky. Cloudy wort, Douglas-fir washbacks and short, broad pot stills all push the spirit toward weight and texture, while carefully chosen yeast and fermentation preserve a fruitier core. For customers, it is a useful contrast to the lighter unpeated style made at Lochranza on the same island.
